text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Moroccan King Hassan II to hold a summit meeting in Rabat today on enhancing efforts to save peace and boosting economic relations. The issue of Jerusalem is among the most important issues in the talks.
- Mubarak tells the Arab parliamentarians' conference that the Arab nation must work hard to achieve an effective formula for an economic block.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says Egypt is concerned over the impact of the Turkish-Israeli military excercises on the peace process.

- Mubarak tells Abu Dhabi television that the military option does not settle any cause. Without solving the issue of Abu Ghneim in Jerusalem, it is difficult to move on the way of peace, Mubarak adds. The common Arab market is necessary so that no other blocks use us, he says.
- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid denies the state is going to privatise the telecommunication sector. The mobile telephone service is the only exception, he adds.

- Mubark says no one can abandon Jerusalem. "We refused to attend a four-party summit meeting because Israel's ambiguous position towards settlement, Mubarak tells chief editors of Egyptian papers on his plane during a flight to Morocco.
